<ul><li><b>Gol</b>: el balón entero pasa:
• Goal: the whole ball crosses the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar.
  • Throw-in if it goes out over a side line; corner if the defending side puts it over their own goal line, and goal kick if the attackers do.
  • Tackles from behind are fouls: free kick to the other team.
  • The goalkeeper (green or yellow) can handle the ball inside their area.
<ul><li>La bola va por el suelo y se jue:
• The ball stays on the ground and is played with the stick. Pass pushes the ball; Hit sends it a long way.
  • A goal only counts if it is shot from inside the circle (the D in front of the goal). From outside, Shoot does a long hit.
  • Tackling from behind is a foul. The goalkeeper wears white pads and a helmet.
  • If it goes over the back line: free hit from 15 m or long corner.
<ul><li><b>Ensayo</b> (5 puntos): llevar:
• Try (5 points): carry the ball over the other team's try line. Then the conversion (2): a kick at the posts from in line with where the try was scored.
  • You carry the ball in your hands and passes can only go backwards or flat; forwards you play it with your foot.
  • Tackle: bring down the ball carrier. A ruck forms and their team nearly always keeps the ball.
  • Drop goal (3): a kick at the posts off the bounce, in open play.
<ul><li>No se puede <b>correr con la pel:
• You can't run with the ball: when you catch it you stop and pass within 3 seconds. No bouncing either.
  • Each player has a position with its letters on the bib (GS, GA, C, GD, GK…) and can only stand in her areas of the court.
  • Only the GS and the GA shoot, from inside the circle. The ring has no backboard.
  • Whoever marks the player with the ball stays 0.9 m (3 feet) away.
  • After every goal there is a centre pass, taken in turns.

<h3>Cómo se juega</h3><ul><li><b>Moverte:
How to play

  • Move: the joystick (drag in the bottom left), the arrow keys or WASD, or the left stick. Up is towards the goal (or try line) you attack.
  • Pass: to the team-mate you point at with the joystick (if you don't point, to the best-placed one). Without the ball, Switch gives you the team-mate nearest the ball. The ball also switches you to the team-mate who receives it.
<li><b>Tiro</b>: mantén y suelta; el ani:
• Shoot: hold and release; the ring is the power. Aim at one side of the goal with the joystick. In the conversion and in netball, the white mark on the ring shows the right power. Without the ball, the same button is Tackle (from the front) or Jump.
  • Sprint: hold it (or Shift, or R2); it uses stamina, which comes back as you jog.
  • View: from behind your player or from the side, like on TV. Leave: two taps.
<li><b>Teclado</b>: Espacio o J pase, K: • Keyboard: Space or J pass, K shoot (hold), Shift sprint, Q switch, V view. Controller: ✕ pass or switch, □ shoot (hold), R2 or R1 sprint, L1 switch, △ view, ○ leave.
<h3>Cómo se lee la pantalla</h3><ul><li>:
Reading the screen

  • Top: the scoreboard (your school on the left, with its colour), the clock for each half and which half it is.
  • Your player has a ring on the ground: white without the ball, yellow with it. A yellow cone above a team-mate: that's where your pass is going. The names are your friends in the room.
<li><b>Abajo</b>: lo que toca hacer ahor:
• Bottom: what to do now. On the map, the pitches in their colour (green football, blue hockey, brown rugby, pink netball) and, during a match, the players: brown the school, the rivals in their colour, white the ball.
  • With the room: whoever invites runs the match and everyone sees the same; each friend plays their own player. «All together» puts you on the same team against the computer; «against each other», on different teams.
